question.text: On the set $R$ of real numbers we define $x P y$ if and only if $x y \geq 0$. Then, the relation $P$ is

options.text: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive

solution.text:
For every real number $x, x^{2} \geq 0$
$\therefore$ $(x, x) \in P$
Hence, $P$ is reflexive.
Now let $(x,y) \in P \\
\Rightarrow xy \geq 0 \\
\Rightarrow yx \geq 0$
$(y, x) \in P$
Hence, $P$ is symmetric. 
Again (-1,0)$\in P$ and (0,2)$\in P$
But (-1,2)$\notin P$
$as(-1)(2)=-2    < 0$
Pis not transitive.
